overall: The Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by giving inadequate notice of the property at issue and by entering executive session after the purchase price was settled; earlier-meeting complaints were untimely, and the AG declined to order nullification of the CPA application.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged inadequate agenda topic specificity for March 14, March 28, April 11, and April 25, 2011 meetings, but were filed more than 30 days after those meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Here, with regard to alleged violations on March 14, 2011; March 28, 2011; April 11, 2011; and April 25, 2011, the complaints were filed more than 30 days after the alleged violations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the May 9 and May 16, 2011 notices listed a land purchase topic without identifying the specific property (48 High Street) with sufficient specificity.
allegations.key_passage: Both notices simply referred to the general type of project, rather than identifying the specific property to be discussed, either by address or by identifying landmarks.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the May 16, 2011 executive session under Purpose 6 (real property purchase) was improper because the price was already agreed and only the deal decision remained.
allegations.key_passage: When the terms of a land purchase have been negotiated and the only remaining discussion relates to whether or not to enter into the deal, Purpose 6 may no longer be used to justify an executive session.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future conduct may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
Publicly release the May 16, 2011 executive session minutes, if not already released, with redactions permitted only under the Public Records Law exemptions or attorney/client privilege.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar conduct may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
